angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 786,837 km at 73.02 pc = 0.14 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 13.6947 +/- 0.0103 mas (same row, RUWE 0.86): 73.02 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.131 +/- 0.0181 solar radii from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1742 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract): 786,837 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.0861 +/- 0.034 solar masses from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1742 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5815 +/- 76 K from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1742 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1742 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1742.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.367, rounded to two decimals
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1742 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.193 dex, from MacDougall et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1742 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.12123, from MacDougall et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1742 (pscomppars): age 3.9 Gyr, from MacDougall et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
